slides.title: How it works
slides.html: OpenDefence Voice signs in to your unit's voice server with ATAK's certificate. You talk in the one net you join, and can listen to other nets too.

slides.title: The voice server
slides.html: Your unit's voice server sits beside its TAK server and holds the nets. OpenDefence Voice finds it through the TAK server ATAK is connected to.

slides.title: No password
slides.html: OpenDefence Voice signs in with ATAK's own certificate, the digital ID you got when you enrolled. There is no password and nothing for you to sign in to.

slides.title: Connects by itself
slides.html: Until ATAK is connected to the TAK server, the pane reads Connect ATAK to the TAK server first and NOT CONNECTED, as here. Then OpenDefence Voice connects by itself.

slides.title: Allow the microphone
slides.html: Your first press to talk shows Allow microphone. Tap it and allow what Android asks.

slides.title: Nets
slides.html: A net is a voice channel on the voice server. Teams/Blue is the net Blue in the group Teams, beside Units, Missions and Roles.

slides.title: Your net
slides.html: You Join one net at a time, and only that net hears you. You pick it from the NET header on the pane.

slides.title: Listening
slides.html: Tick Listen to hear another net without joining it. The Listening line under the PTT names the nets you hear, and who talks in one.

slides.title: Heard with no setup
slides.html: With no setup, OpenDefence Voice listens to Missions/Guard, the mission nets open to you and the nets of your ATAK team and role.

slides.title: Talking
slides.html: You talk in your net with push-to-talk (PTT) or with voice activation (VOX).

slides.title: Push-to-talk
slides.html: Push-to-talk (PTT) means you talk while you hold a button and stop when you let go. HOLD TO TX on the pane is your PTT and needs no setup.

slides.title: Other PTT buttons
slides.html: A Bluetooth PTT button, a headset's talk button or volume up works once set up in Settings. The Active Key on Samsung XCover and Tab Active models needs no setup.

slides.title: VOX
slides.html: VOX needs no press: it sends any sound loud enough at your headset's microphone, under your name. It is off until you turn it on in Settings.

slides.title: Who is there
slides.html: OpenDefence Voice shows who is in your net and who is talking. Here BRAVO2 joins your net, then talks.

slides.title: Who is in your net
slides.html: The number beside the PTT is how many are in your net, here 2. Tap it for their names.

slides.title: Who is talking
slides.html: While someone in your net talks, their name shows in blue under NET, as BRAVO2 does here.

slides.title: Your name in the net
slides.html: Others see you by the name you were enrolled with, from your certificate. It can differ from your callsign in ATAK.

slides.title: The status line
slides.html: The line under OD Voice says how OpenDefence Voice is connected, here Connected with a green dot.

slides.title: What the dot means
slides.html: Green means Connected, amber that it is connecting or retrying by itself. Red means you must act, grey that it is off or not connected.

slides.title: The user manual
slides.html: User manual, under HELP in ATAK's OD Voice Preferences, lists every message and what to do.
